predecessors.note: Cliopatria's first year for the row is 1294; the page does not say that the city was a state of its own in 1294.

land.text: Nizhny Novgorod, 'incorporated into the Grand Principality of Moscow in 1392'

successors.note: Cliopatria's Moscow shape holds Cliopatria's own Nizhny disc from 1395 (22 of 22 cells); the Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod principality behind the city is larger and has no dossier.

capitals.name: Nizhny Novgorod
capitals.note: 'The seat of the powerful Suzdal Principality was moved there from Gorodets in 1350.' Before 1350 the city is the polity's only place.

correction.text: a disc of 42 km (the 5,416 km2 of Cliopatria's shape) round the city, at 44.0 E, 56.3 N

keyframe_review.note: 5,416 km2 (22 cells) for 1294-1384, but centred at 42.49 E, 56.58 N, about 90 km west-north-west of the city (43.998 E, 56.335 N in the gazetteer); the two do not touch. The page names the city, not a boundary, and no area. The disc is moved onto the city; the principality itself was larger (Moscow's 1395 shape holds about 300 more cells east of Suzdal that belonged to it) but no page opened gives an extent.

correction.text: the same disc round the city, valid 1385-1391

keyframe_review.note: Same 22 cells as 1294, displaced as above. The page ends the state in 1392 ('incorporation into the Grand Principality of Moscow in 1392'); Cliopatria keeps the shape to 1394, so 1392-1394 are Moscow's (Vasily I page: taken over in 1393 'With Tokhtamysh's permission').

region.text: the city of Nizhny Novgorod and its district

ledger.note: 1294 (Cliopatria's first year): Nizhny Novgorod appears as a polity of its own. The page: founded 4 February 1221 by Prince Yuri II of Vladimir; 'incorporated into the Vladimir-Suzdal Principality in 1264'; it gives no status for 1294-1394, so the start is Cliopatria's.

1350: the seat of the Suzdal Principality moves from Gorodets to Nizhny Novgorod. 'The seat of the powerful Suzdal Principality was moved there from Gorodets in 1350'; Dmitry Konstantinovich (1323-1383) 'sought to make his capital a rival worthy of Moscow'. From here the polity is the capital of the Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod principality; no land change is given.

region.text: Nizhny Novgorod, 'incorporated into the Grand Principality of Moscow in 1392'

ledger.note: 1392: Nizhny Novgorod is incorporated into Moscow. 'After the city's incorporation into the Grand Principality of Moscow in 1392, the local princes took the name Shuysky.' The Moscow page: 'Vasily was given permission to take the throne of Nizhny Novgorod' (1392); the Vasily I page: 'With Tokhtamysh's permission, Vasily I took over' in 1393. Cliopatria's Moscow shape holds the land from 1395.
1392: the principality ends in Moscow's hands; its land goes to the Grand Principality of Moscow.

certainty.note: The page gives a city and a principality's seat, not a boundary; the extent is approximate.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Nizhny Novgorod' row (1294-1394, two identical 5,416 km2 shapes) is a city-sized disc displaced about 90 km west of the city, and no other Cliopatria shape covers the city at any date, so the dossier moves the disc onto the city. What the pages describe is the Principality of Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod (seat moved to the city in 1350, taken by Moscow in 1392), which has no Cliopatria row and no dossier: counterparts_needing_dossiers 'principality-of-suzdal-nizhny-novgorod' 1350-1392 (the 1341 creation date and the princes Konstantin Vasilyevich, Dmitry Konstantinovich and Boris are not on the pages opened). The first fetch of https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suzdal_Principality failed (url_not_found); https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principality_of_Suzdal loaded as the Vladimir-Suzdal article and has nothing on Nizhny Novgorod beyond the 1360-1363 interruption. The start 1294 is Cliopatria's; the page has the city inside the Vladimir-Suzdal principality from 1264 (confidence 1 on the found event). The state label might be better 'Principality of Suzdal-Nizhny Novgorod' from 1350.
